jobs.name: memory-audit
jobs.prompt:
Audit persistent memory. In order:
1. Report current usage percentages for MEMORY.md and USER.md (chars vs limits 2200 and 1375).
2. For each memory entry stamped [verified YYYY-MM-DD] older than 90 days, re-verify it with a shell command. Update the stamp if still true; use memory remove if false; report both lists.
3. Flag any entry that a single shell command could answer — those are Tier D, not memory. Propose removals, do not apply them.
4. If MEMORY.md usage is above 80%, merge overlapping entries with memory replace.
5. Report what changed in under 10 lines.

jobs.name: kwin-68-pacing-fix-watch
jobs.prompt:
You are checking whether the KWin PipeWire screencast frame-pacing fix (KDE bug 524129 — uneven frame timing with 120Hz display + 60fps variable-rate capture, fixed by nanosecond deadlines + fixed interval in kwin screencaststream.cpp, and Sunshine PR 5538 support) has arrived on this Nobara 44 desktop.

Steps:
1. Run: rpm -q kwin — note the version.
2. Check installed kwin changelog: rpm -q --changelog kwin | grep -im5 -E '524129|screencast|pacing' | head -10
3. Optionally check https://updates.nobaraproject.org/updates.txt (terminal curl) for any plasma 6.8 mention.
4. Also check kwin source availability: if kwin version >= 6.8, the fix is in.

Then compose a SHORT telegram message for Jitin (non-technical, plain language, no jargon):

You can also remove the temporary mitigation in ~/.config/sunshine/sunshine.conf (lines: minimum_fps_target=40, nvenc_twopass=quarter_res) — or just tell Hermes to do it.'

Your final response IS the telegram message. Keep it under 120 words.

jobs.name: stream-lock-report-delivery
jobs.prompt:
One-shot delivery job, no research needed. Compose a final response that delivers EXACTLY the report text below (plain text, no additions or edits beyond light formatting), then stop. Do not run tools.

--- REPORT START ---
KEEP THE MOONLIGHT STREAM UP WHILE LOCKING THE DESKTOP — RESEARCH FINDINGS

Short answer: yes, but not by using the normal lock screen. On KDE Plasma Wayland (your setup), locking the session is a security wall — KWin freezes the normal PipeWire screencast and Sunshine's kwin capture goes black. The trick is to lock down everything EXCEPT the output being streamed. Three proven approaches:

OPTION 1 — VIRTUAL DISPLAY + DPMS OFF ON THE PHYSICAL MONITOR (best fit, you are already 90% set up)
Your Sunshine already streams a virtual output ('Virtual-sunshine') via krfb-virtualmonitor with capture=kwin. Because the capture is tied to the virtual output, the physical monitor is NOT part of the stream at all. So:
- On connect (extend your global_prep_cmd 'do' hook): turn the physical monitor off with kscreen-doctor --dpms off, and optionally lock the session is NOT possible (see option 2) — instead set the physical monitor to show nothing.
- KWin keeps the virtual output active because your stream holds a screencast + you already mitigate idle via minimum_fps_target; also hold a screensaver inhibitor (kde-inhibit --screenSaver) so PowerDevil doesn't kill the capture.
- Result: the physical monitor shows black / nothing, the stream on the laptop stays perfectly live. Anyone at the desk sees a dark screen. Keyboard/mouse at the desk still work though — that is the one caveat of this option.
- Sources: github.com/RomeoRD/kwin-sunshine-vdisplay, github.com/jhonsnake/sunshine-kde-virtual-display, LizardByte/Sunshine issue #5209 (kwin/portal capture keeps working when the physical monitor is off — it is KMS autodetect that fails).

OPTION 2 — A SECOND LOCKED-SESSION-STYLE USER (the true 'lock everything but the stream' setup)
KDE's lock screen and an active screencast are mutually exclusive by design (Wayland treats screencast as privileged, lock cuts it off — see KDE bug tracker and universal-blue forum reports of PipeWire capture dying on lock). To get a genuine lock while the stream lives:
- Run the stream in a SEPARATE session: either a second user account whose session owns only the virtual monitor (headless), or a dedicated headless compositor (e.g. Sway) just for Sunshine. Reference implementation: github.com/daaaaan/sunshine-headless-sway — full input isolation via udev rules hiding Sunshine's virtual input devices from the host desktop, separate PipeWire null sink so even audio is isolated, while your main KDE session can be locked as usual.
- Your main desktop is then locked normally (Win+L equivalent) and nobody at the desk can see or touch anything; the stream keeps running untouched.
- Tradeoff: more moving parts — separate session, udev rules, audio routing.

OPTION 3 — LIGHTWEIGHT HYBRID (least effort, ~90% of the benefit)
- Keep everything as is.
- Add to the connect hook: kscreen-doctor --dpms off on the physical output, plus a dbus screensaver inhibit for the stream duration.
- Add a KDE shortcut (System Settings > Shortcuts) or a small script that locks the session when you are DONE streaming — so privacy at the desk is protected by turning the panel off, and the real lock happens only when the stream ends.
- On disconnect (undo hook): kscreen-doctor --dpms on to wake the physical monitor before anything else.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK (tried and documented by many)
- Locking the session and expecting the stream to continue: on KDE Wayland the capture goes black/frozen — by security design (Wayland portal model, LizardByte issue #4448 documents the Windows equivalent; NixOS wiki notes Sunshine cannot even wake a locked display).
- Streaming through an RDP-style locked desktop: moonlight-docs wiki Troubleshooting documents that a technically locked machine blocks Sunshine apps from starting.

RECOMMENDATION FOR KURAMA-CORE
Option 1 + the disconnect-lock from Option 3: extend stream-display / your global_prep_cmd to (a) inhibit screensaver+DPMS for the virtual output only, (b) kscreen-doctor --dpms off the physical panel on connect, (c) dpms on + lock session on disconnect. That gives you: dark screen at the desk, untouched live stream on the laptop, and a locked desktop the moment you disconnect. The desk input caveat (keyboard/mouse still live) can be closed later with the udev input-isolation trick from the headless-sway project if you ever want it.

KEY LINKS
- https://github.com/RomeoRD/kwin-sunshine-vdisplay
- https://github.com/jhonsnake/sunshine-kde-virtual-display
- https://github.com/daaaaan/sunshine-headless-sway
- https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/issues/5209
- https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/issues/4448
- https://www.reddit.com/r/MoonlightStreaming/comments/1tg1dnc/guide_sunshine_on_kde_wayland_virtual_display/
--- REPORT END ---

jobs.name: desk-lock-plan-ready
jobs.prompt:
One-shot delivery job, no tools needed. Send EXACTLY this message as your final response, then stop.

DESK-LOCK PLAN READY

Your question: keep the Moonlight stream as-is while locking the rest of the desktop. Short answer from the research: a normal lock screen can't do it (KDE's lock screen would cover the stream itself), so the plan locks the desk a different way:

- The panel already goes dark during streams (existing setup).
- NEW: while a stream runs, the desk keyboard and mouse get locked out at the driver level (a tiny daemon grabs the physical input devices; crashes release them automatically, so it can never wedge you).
- Moonlight input on the laptop is injected differently and stays fully live — the stream is untouched.
- Optional (off by default): automatically lock the whole session with a password after a stream ends.

Why not a lock screen: with only one screen enabled, the lock screen IS what gets streamed (documented OBS behavior), lock/wake transitions freeze screen capture, and Plasma 6.6 removed per-monitor screen-off. Full evidence chain is in the plan.

Plan file: ~/Work/streamer/desk-lock-plan.md (committed, bbe76b9). 6 tasks, tests in the repo's existing style, escape hatches documented (Tailscale SSH recovery always available). Say the word and it gets built.
